# Repeated-measures within-group ANOVA power calculation
# Following G*Power's rm_within design specification

# User-specified parameters
partial_eta_sq <- 0.08
k <- 3  # number of time points
rho <- 0.5  # compound symmetry correlation
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
epsilon <- 1  # sphericity assumption satisfied

# Step 1: Convert partial eta-squared to f
# f^2 = eta^2 / (1 - eta^2)
f_sq <- partial_eta_sq / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
f <- sqrt(f_sq)

cat("Effect Size Conversion:\n")
cat(sprintf("Partial η² = %.4f\n", partial_eta_sq))
cat(sprintf("f² = η²/(1−η²) = %.4f/(%.4f) = %.6f\n", partial_eta_sq, 1-partial_eta_sq, f_sq))
cat(sprintf("f = √(f²) = %.6f\n\n", f))

# Step 2: Define the noncentral parameter formula
# In G*Power's rm_within ANOVA: λ = f² × n × (k − 1) × (1 − ρ)
# df1 = k - 1 = 2
# df2 = (k - 1) × (n - 1) = 2 × (n - 1)

# Step 3: Function to calculate power for given n
calc_power <- function(n, f_sq, k, rho, alpha) {
  df1 <- k - 1
  df2 <- (k - 1) * (n - 1)
  
  # Noncentral parameter (accounting for correlation structure)
  lambda <- f_sq * n * (k - 1) * (1 - rho)
  
  # Critical F value at alpha
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | H1) = 1 - CDF(f_crit; df1, df2, lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  
  return(list(n = n, power = power, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, lambda = lambda, f_crit = f_crit))
}

# Step 4: Find minimum sample size via binary search and exhaustive check
cat("Searching for minimum sample size achieving target power ≥ 0.90:\n\n")

# Start with a reasonable range
n_min <- 1
n_max <- 500

results_table <- data.frame()

# Test values from 1 to 200 to find the crossing point
for (n in 1:200) {
  result <- calc_power(n, f_sq, k, rho, alpha)
  results_table <- rbind(results_table, data.frame(
    n = n,
    power = result$power,
    df1 = result$df1,
    df2 = result$df2,
    lambda = result$lambda
  ))
  
  if (n <= 20 || n %% 10 == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("n=%3d: power=%.6f, df1=%d, df2=%3d, λ=%.6f\n", 
                n, result$power, result$df1, result$df2, result$lambda))
  }
}

# Find minimum n achieving target power
min_idx <- which(results_table$power >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- results_table$n[min_idx]
achieved_power <- results_table$power[min_idx]

cat("\n" %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "\n")
cat(sprintf("MINIMUM SAMPLE SIZE: n = %d participants\n", min_n))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at n=%d: %.6f (%.4f%%)\n", min_n, achieved_power, achieved_power*100))

  prev_result <- calc_power(min_n - 1, f_sq, k, rho, alpha)
  cat(sprintf("Power at n=%d (preceding): %.6f (%.4f%%)\n", min_n-1, prev_result$power, prev_result$power*100))
}

cat("="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "="  %+% "\n\n")

# Final verification with detailed computation

cat("Final Verification (n = " %+% min_n %+% "):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Partial η² = %.6f\n", partial_eta_sq))
cat(sprintf("  f = %.6f\n", f))

cat(sprintf("  ρ (compound symmetry) = %.4f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("  df₁ = k − 1 = %d\n", final_result$df1))

cat(sprintf("  λ = f² × n × (k − 1) × (1 − ρ) = %.6f\n", final_result$lambda))
cat(sprintf("  Critical F (α=0.05) = %.6f\n", final_result$f_crit))
cat(sprintf("  Power (1 − β) = %.6f\n\n", final_result$power))

    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(achieved_power, 6), unit = "probability"),

), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)
